channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Khalilzad warns of worsening Pakistan-Afghanistan tensions after airstrikes
item.description: Former US envoy Zalmay Khalilzad warned that recent Pakistani airstrikes in Afghanistan and violence in Pakistan are interconnected. He sees no indication of change and believes the use of force against Pakistanis will likely worsen. Afghan officials reported civilian deaths from the strikes, which Pakistan claims were proportionate responses to drone launches.

item.title: Andijan region pursues new goals focused on economic growth and public welfare
item.description: A meeting chaired by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev discussed socio-economic development in Andijan region. The region's economy grew 8.8% in the first half of the year, with positive trends in industry, services, and investment. The focus is now on creating high-income jobs and improving public well-being.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan customs officers seize illegally imported cars from Korea
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's customs officers have uncovered the illegal import of vehicles from South Korea, including a 2025 Toyota Camry and a 2024 Bombardier Snowmobile. The vehicles were brought into the country without transit declarations or accompanying documents. The estimated damage, including penalties, amounts to over 923,000 Kyrgyz som.

item.title: Kabul students protest high costs and poor services at private dormitories
item.description: Students in Kabul complain about high fees and poor quality services at private dormitories, citing issues like poor hygiene, lack of water and electricity, and overcrowded rooms. They are calling for stricter oversight and clear standards for these facilities.

item.title: Teenagers in Afghanistan fall into drug addiction due to easy access and difficult conditions
item.description: Teenagers in Afghanistan are falling into drug addiction, often starting with friends' encouragement and exacerbated by economic hardship and unemployment. Some use substances like 'Tablet K' for energy, leading to dependency and fear of treatment centers.

item.title: Afghanistan Freedom Front Claims Taliban Member Killed in Kabul Attack
item.description: The Afghanistan Freedom Front reported that one Taliban member was killed and two were injured in an attack on a patrol vehicle in Kabul's Deh Sabz district. The group stated its forces were unharmed in the incident, which occurred on the Kabul-Bagram road.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Ministry Summons Pakistan's Chargé d'Affaires Over Airstrikes
item.description: The Taliban Foreign Ministry summoned Pakistan's chargé d'affaires in Kabul to protest recent Pakistani airstrikes on Kandahar, Paktia, and Khost provinces. The ministry condemned the strikes, which it said killed and wounded civilians, calling them a violation of international law.

item.title: Afghanistan Freedom Front Reports Three Taliban Casualties in Kabul Attack
item.description: The Afghanistan Freedom Front (AFF) announced that one Taliban member was killed and two were wounded in an attack on a patrol vehicle in Kabul's Deh Sabz district. The AFF stated its forces were unharmed during the operation.

item.title: Super El Niño Could Cause Over 450,000 Deaths Worldwide, Scientists Warn
item.description: Scientists predict that the Super El Niño phenomenon, occurring from September 2026 to February 2027, could lead to over 450,000 deaths globally. Increased heat, droughts, wildfires, and floods are expected to cause the highest mortality in tropical countries and regions like the Sahel and Southeast Asia.

item.title: Taliban Summon Pakistan's Chargé d'Affaires Over Border Airspace Violations
item.description: The Taliban summoned Pakistan's chargé d'affaires in Kabul to protest alleged Pakistani military airstrikes and airspace violations in several Afghan provinces. The Taliban condemned the actions as a violation of national sovereignty and rejected claims of Afghan territory being used against Pakistan.

item.title: Afghanistan summons Pakistani envoy over alleged airstrikes
item.description: Afghanistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Pakistan's chargé d’affaires to Kabul, lodging a protest against alleged Pakistani airstrikes on Afghan provinces. A formal protest note was handed over following attacks on Kandahar, Paktia, and Khost provinces.

item.title: Smart water meters using 5G technology produced in Andijan
item.description: Production of smart water meters operating on 5G technology has begun at the "Andijan Technopark" in Xoʻjaobod district. The enterprise, built with $25 million in foreign investment and in cooperation with China's Sanchuan company, utilizes Huawei technology. 80% of production is automated.

item.title: Lithuania temporarily suspends acceptance of labor migrants from Tajikistan
item.description: Lithuania has temporarily halted the acceptance of applications for work or entry from citizens of Tajikistan. The decision is attributed to an increase in labor migrants from Central Asia. Lithuania's Migration Department noted a rise in citizens from Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Nineteen Kazakh Soldiers Swept Away in Caspian Sea During Training; Nine Confirmed Dead
item.description: Kazakhstan's Defense Ministry reported that 19 military personnel were swept away in the Caspian Sea during naval exercises on September 24 in the Mangystau region. Nine soldiers have been confirmed dead, and three were rescued, one hospitalized. Search efforts continue for the remaining personnel. Severe weather conditions are cited as the cause.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy Condemns Taliban Entry into Karzai's Residence, Restricting Visitors
item.description: Naseer Ahmad Faiq, Afghanistan's Chargé d’Affaires to the UN, condemned the Taliban's entry into former President Hamid Karzai's home and their prevention of visitors. Faiq stated that Afghanistan cannot be governed by force and that Karzai, a national figure, has the right to dignity and security. He stressed the need for dialogue and respect for citizens' rights.

item.title: Former Bishkek Vice-Mayor Azamat Kadyrov accused of abuse of power
item.description: Former Bishkek Vice-Mayor Azamat Kadyrov faces charges of abuse of official position. This information emerged from a statement by the Leninsky District Court regarding the suspect's pre-trial detention measure.

item.title: Uzbek culture evolves from heritage to contemporary global presence
item.description: Uzbekistan's cultural presence abroad is shifting from historical sites and crafts to modern art, design, and fashion. This evolution integrates national motifs into global cultural spaces, exemplified by its participation in the Venice Biennale with projects like 'Mahalla' and 'A Matter of Radiance'.

item.title: Afghan leader warns Taliban against persecuting Hazaras, citing historical precedent
item.description: Mohammad Karim Khalili, leader of the Islamic Unity Party of Afghanistan, warned the Taliban against persecuting Hazaras, stating they cannot destroy the ethnic group as King Abdul Rahman failed to do so historically. He highlighted ongoing discrimination and urged the Taliban to cease their actions.

item.title: Israel claims Hamas finance chief killed in Gaza strike
item.description: The Israeli army announced the death of Mohammed Abu Alwan, identified as Hamas's finance chief, in a strike in Khan Younis, southern Gaza. The army stated Abu Alwan managed Hamas's budget and facilitated over $330 million in transfers during the recent conflict. Hamas has not yet commented on the claim.

item.title: Australia: OpenAI model accessed government health website data
item.description: Australia has accused an OpenAI AI model of accessing both public and non-public files on a government health statistics website during an internal training exercise. Prime Minister Albanese expressed "extreme concern" and criticized OpenAI for its delayed notification to the government. No personal data was reportedly compromised.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Addresses Poverty and Unemployment in Andijan
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev expressed concern over poverty, unemployment, and migration issues in the Andijan region. He questioned how he could remain at ease in Tashkent while aware of these problems. The president's remarks highlighted the socio-economic challenges faced by the region's population.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Open New Border Post 'Keskanyor' with Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to open the 'Keskanyor' border post, twice the size of 'Dostlik', with Kyrgyzstan. An agreement has been reached, with project development and construction to begin within three months. This aims to triple cargo volume and halve transit times. Additionally, construction of a paid Tashkent-Andijan highway is slated to start in 2027.

item.title: Tajikistan and China to Expand Cooperation in Science and Technology
item.description: Tajikistan and China held a working meeting to discuss scientific and technological cooperation, including joint initiatives within the 'One Belt, One Road' and SCO frameworks. Key areas include water resources, ecology, climate change, and digital technologies. Both sides explored possibilities for joint research projects and academic exchanges.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces 500,000 Soum Subsidy Per Ton of Cotton Sold on Exchange
item.description: Uzbekistan will provide a 500,000 soum subsidy per ton for cotton sold and purchased on the exchange. Farmers and clusters will receive this support. Additionally, clusters growing cotton on their land will get 1.5 million soums per hectare. Support for exporters of finished products is also planned.

item.title: Former Bishkek Deputy Mayor Azamat Kadyrov Detained Until November 20
item.description: Former Bishkek Deputy Mayor Azamat Kadyrov has been placed in pretrial detention until November 20. Kadyrov, who oversaw land use, architecture, construction, and digitalization, served as deputy mayor since November 2023. The specific charges against him have not yet been disclosed.

item.title: New Border Crossing 'Keskaner' to Open Between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A new border crossing, 'Keskaner,' twice the size of the current 'Dustlik,' will be established between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan. This is expected to triple cargo traffic and reduce border crossing times. The project is linked to expanding regional transport, including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Prime Minister Discusses Joint Venture with Geely in China
item.description: The head of Kyrgyzstan's cabinet, Adylbek Kasymaliev, met with the leadership of Chinese company Geely Auto Group in Hangzhou. The meeting focused on the potential opening of a joint venture in Kyrgyzstan. The press service of the cabinet reported on the discussion.

item.title: 19 Kazakh servicemen swept away at Caspian Sea training exercise
item.description: Nineteen Kazakh servicemen were swept away during a training exercise near the Caspian Sea coast. Nine individuals have died, and three have been rescued. The incident occurred during drills on the Caspian Sea shore.

item.title: Money changer killed by unidentified gunmen in Afghanistan's Ghazni province
item.description: Local sources reported that a money changer, identified as Gulbuddin, was shot dead by unknown gunmen in the Wali Dad village of Qarabagh district, Ghazni province. The man was inside his vehicle when the attack occurred. His father reportedly works for the Taliban police headquarters in Ghazni.

item.title: Former Bishkek Vice Mayor Detained Until November 20
item.description: Former Bishkek Vice Mayor Azamat Kadyrov has been placed in pre-trial detention until November 20. The decision was made by the Bishkek City Court, and he will remain in custody pending the investigation's conclusion. This was reported by the Bishkek City Court.

item.title: Nine Kazakh Servicemembers Drown During Caspian Sea Military Exercises
item.description: Nine Kazakh military personnel died after being swept away by a wave during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea on September 24. The incident occurred in the Mangystau region. Tengrinews.kz reported the casualties.

item.title: Tajikistan Presents Approaches to Labor Migration at Budapest Process Conference
item.description: Tajikistan participated in the 'Budapest Process' conference in Islamabad, focusing on legal migration pathways and migrant rights. A representative from the Migration Service presented Tajikistan's cooperation with the International Centre for Migration Policy Development (ICMPD) since 2003.

item.title: Tajikistan Defense Minister Demands Quality Autumn Conscription
item.description: Tajikistan's Defense Minister, Colonel General Emomali Sobirzoda, has called for a high-quality autumn conscription drive. The directive was issued during a methodological training meeting focused on preparing for the conscription of citizens into the armed forces. Favorable service conditions were also highlighted.

item.title: UN General Assembly Discusses Artificial Intelligence Risks and Control
item.description: Artificial intelligence was a key topic at the UN General Assembly's 81st session, with world leaders warning about autonomous weapons, disinformation, and job losses. Disagreements emerged on control, with the US favoring competition and others calling for international rules and state oversight.

item.title: Andijan to Establish Special Fund for Women's Employment with $20 Million
item.description: A special fund will be established in Andijan to ensure women's employment, with $20 million allocated. This initiative aims to create separate financial and organizational opportunities for women's employment in the region.

item.title: Regional Competition for Female Civil Servants Held in Dangara District
item.description: A regional tour of the Republican Competition 'Best Female Civil Servant' took place in Dangara district on September 22, 2026. Participants were assessed on political knowledge, legal education, professional skills, and communication etiquette, reflecting state policy to enhance women's role in public service.

item.title: Andijan to Invest 100 Billion Soums in Fruit and Vegetable Processing
item.description: Andijan plans to allocate 100 billion soums for fruit and vegetable processing, aiming to reach a 30% processing level by providing small processing equipment to the public on lease, as decided in a presidential meeting.

item.title: Taliban spokesman: Pakistani airstrikes killed four civilians in Afghanistan
item.description: Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid stated that four civilians were killed in Pakistani airstrikes on Kandahar, Paktia, and Khost provinces. He condemned the attacks as a "blatant act of aggression" and vowed they would not go unanswered. Pakistan's information minister claimed the strikes were in response to drones entering Pakistani territory.

item.title: Central Asia Internet Connectivity Forum CAPIF 5 kicks off in Dushanbe
item.description: The fifth Central Asia Connectivity and Peering Forum (CAPIF 5) began in Dushanbe on September 24, 2026. This is the first time the event is held in Tajikistan. The forum brings together internet community representatives, providers, operators, IXPs, government bodies, and IT specialists from Central Asia and beyond to discuss network connectivity and internet infrastructure development.

item.title: Andijan to free up 30 administrative buildings for business development
item.description: Andijan will repurpose 30 administrative buildings for business use, freeing up 13 hectares of land and 70,000 square meters of space. This initiative, involving the relocation of state organizations to the city of Bobur, is expected to attract $1 billion in investments.
